Workload-aware batching defaults (Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient) — design ## Overview This document defines Redwood Runtime’s “workload-aware batching defaults”: three customer-facing latency SLO tiers (Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient) implemented as tiered batching profiles selected automatically by the runtime based on workload signals and policy configuration. The primary goal is to reduce cost per 1K tokens via safer batching defaults while preserving predictable tail latency (especially for streaming) and avoiding starvation under mixed workloads. This is the primary design doc for: - Tier definitions and the contract we uphold for each tier (in runtime terms). - Scheduler knob mapping (continuous batching heuristics, queueing, prefill/decode balancing, admission control). - Workload signals (length buckets, streaming flag, concurrency, overload signals) and selection logic. - Override hierarchy (customer override > route/model policy > tier default) and explainability (reason codes). - Rollout and rollback plan for Hosted and Dedicated. ## Background and decision summary We will ship three tiered defaults rather than per-tenant real-time autotuning (see ADR-023). The tiers give customers a stable mental model and enable us to publish and validate recommended profiles per model family + hardware class. Key principles: 1) Tail latency is a first-class constraint (Fast tier must protect p99 and streaming “time-to-first-token”). 2) Defaults must be explainable (operators can see the effective tier/profile and why it was selected). 3) Behavior under overload must be safe and predictable (backpressure, load shedding, and bounded queues). 4) Profiles must work under mixed workloads (avoid starving long prompts, avoid “short prompts dominate forever”).
